label: Belief that God exists: Assenting to the existence of the relevant personal God
definition: Assenting to the existence of the relevant personal God. Nonbelief includes doubt and suspension, as well as outright denial. Belief is distinct from knowledge, certainty, felt presence, accepting a relationship, and voluntary control over belief. Belief may be false in a non-theistic interpretation.
note: Explicit interpretation vocabulary for #252. Source claims retain their own pinned locators; these records do not add axioms or establish the truth of the interpreted predicates.

formal_gap.meaning: Sig.Believes w p t says that, at world w, person p assents at time t to the existence of the relevant personal God. Nonbelief includes doubt and suspension as well as denial. It is a field of the hiddenness signature (TruthCore.Hiddenness.Vocabulary.Sig, #252), indexed by world, person and time and supplied by each interpretation; worlds carry no modal accessibility laws.
examples: A person who assents that a personal God exists, whether or not that belief is true.
exclusions: Knowledge, certainty, felt presence and voluntary control over belief.
open_obligations: ConceptNeeded (no belief without the concept) and AccessNeedsBelief (no conscious access without belief) are open premises that constrain it.
Belief may be false under a non-theistic interpretation; nothing makes it factive.
These records add no axioms; whether the interpreted predicate holds of real persons is not established by any finite model.
No formalization candidate: belief is an interpreted psychological input.
